newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on new Brazil soy purchase.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on new Brazil soy purchase.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower on Thursday, hit by news a U.S. processor bought Brazilian soybeans for import into the United States, traders said.

An Owensboro Grain official confirmed the purchase of 150,000 tonnes optional-origin soybeans. He said the beans could come from the U.S., Brazil, Argentina or Paraguay at the seller's option. Trade sources speculated they would buy from Brazil because supplies were cheaper and of better quality.
The timing of the deal was especially bearish for the market which was still reeling from Tuesday's USDA report, traders said. The report put ending stocks above expectations.

USDA said U.S. exports would fall when cheaper, abundant Brazilian supplies hit the market. News of the Owensboro purchase confirmed ideas U.S. prices were too high, even for domestic buyers, traders said.

"This market is still showing a negative tone left from yesterday's heavy break," Jason Roose, analyst with U.S. Commodities, said. "South American prices are a lot cheaper and we're coming into harvest (in Brazil). At these high levels, are we going to be competitive?"
Soybeans ended 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower to unchanged with May flat at $8.28-1/2 a bushel.
Still, some traders suggested the soybeans would not come from Brazil because U.S. basis levels would slip, making it unprofitable to import Brazilian supplies.
"I don't think the beans ever will arrive here, they probably will be diverted or canceled," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter. "But still some say Brazil could sell 150,000 tonnes to the U.S."

New crop November was pressured by news IMC Global Inc, a major fertilizer firm expected U.S. soy acreage to reach 66 million acres, above USDA's outlook for 65.3 million which was issued at an outlook conference in February. IMC said its survey of U.S. planting intentions indicated farmers would plant 66 million acres of soybeans and 81 million of corn.

Traders also cited rumors a private analytical firm would release its acreage estimates on Friday. The report was expected to show soybean acreage estimates above USDA and IMC estimates, floor sources said.
Soybean volume was estimated by the CBOT at 80,000 contracts compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 107,755.
On the day, FIMAT Futures sold five million bushesl November, Prudential Securities sold five million July and Cargill Inc bought three million July, traders said.

In options trade, Continental Grain and Cargill Investor Services each bought 1,000 July $8.75 calls and sold 1,000 July $9.75 calls at 16-1/2 to 17 cents, floor sources said. Louis Dreyfus reportedly bought 1,300 November $7.00 puts at 34-1/2 to 35 cents, traders said.
